parts.name: ecgmonitor
parts.what: A bedside patient monitor seen from the front: dark screen with a glowing green ECG trace sweeping left to right (drawn by a moving pen, erasing ahead like a real monitor), a heart-rate box on the right showing the rate as digits, a small pulsing heart icon. Reusable for every resuscitation, cardiology and ICU lesson.
events: vf — the rhythm degenerates into ventricular fibrillation: fast chaotic irregular squiggle, rate box shows dashes, screen edge flashes red
flatline — the trace goes flat (asystole), rate shows 0, everything dims except a flat green line
shock — a bright white-blue flash across the screen with a single tall spike artefact
rosc — a normal sinus rhythm returns (regular PQRST complexes), rate box shows a normal value, heart icon beats again
parts.accuracy: ECG shapes: normal sinus rhythm = regular P wave, narrow QRS spike, T wave; VF = chaotic irregular waveform without identifiable complexes; asystole = flat line. Default state: normal sinus rhythm ~75/min. Monitor colours: dark screen, green ECG (medical convention).

parts.name: aed
parts.what: An automated external defibrillator: a rounded bright (green or yellow) case with a handle, a large shock button with a lightning-bolt symbol, a small screen, and two electrode pads connected by cables. Reusable for BLS/AED lessons.
events: pads — the two pads unfold/slide out on their cables
charge — the device charges: the shock button glows and pulses brighter and faster, a charge bar fills on the screen
shock — the button flashes, an energy burst travels along both cables to the pads
parts.accuracy: AED: pads placed on the bare chest, the device analyses the rhythm and advises a shock; a shock button with a lightning bolt symbol is the universal convention. No brand names or text on the device.

parts.name: cpr
parts.what: Chest compressions seen from the side: a patient's chest (torso in profile, lying flat) with a rescuer's two stacked hands (heel of the hand) on the centre of the chest and straight arms from above. Reusable for every CPR lesson.
events: compress — rhythmic compressions start: hands push the chest down and let it fully recoil, at 100 to 120 per minute (about 2 compressions per second at 30 fps = one every ~16 frames), a small depth arrow shows the push; blood-flow pulse glow from the heart area on each push
stop — compressions stop, hands rest
parts.accuracy: High-quality CPR (AHA 2025): rate 100 to 120 per minute, full chest recoil between compressions, hands on the centre of the chest (lower half of the sternum), arms straight. Depth for adults at least 5 cm — show a clear push but no numbers on screen.

parts.name: timer
parts.what: A countdown ring: a large circular progress ring (like a stopwatch bezel) with minutes:seconds digits in the centre (Html text, digits only), counting down from 3:00. Reusable wherever a lesson needs time pressure.
events: start — the ring starts sweeping and the digits count down (1 real second per second at 30 fps; the ring colour shifts from teal to amber to red as it runs)
stop — the countdown freezes and the ring settles green
parts.accuracy: Starts at 3:00 (the handbook's 'first three minutes'). Digits only, no words.

parts.name: ward
parts.what: A hospital ward bay at night, side view, wide (about 1600×700): floor line, a hospital bed (adjustable frame, wheels, raised head section, pillow) with a patient asleep under a blanket (head on pillow, face in profile), an IV pole with a drip bag and line to the patient's arm, a privacy curtain on a ceiling rail at one side, a window with a night sky and a crescent moon, a wall oxygen/suction panel above the bed head. Calm, quiet, beautiful; flat colours that also read on a dark stage. Reusable for any in-hospital lesson.
events: alarm — a red alarm light pulses across the bay (red wash on the wall and bed, pulsing ~2 per second), the patient's face goes pale
calm — the red wash fades and a soft warm night light returns
parts.accuracy: Standard adult hospital bed and bay equipment; no text or brand.

parts.name: chain
parts.what: A horizontal chain of interlocking oval links (like a real metal chain, flat-illustrated), data.n links (3–8, default 6), each link large enough to hold a small icon slot in its centre (leave the centre empty; labels are added by the lesson). Reusable: the Chain of Survival, any sequence where every step depends on the previous one.
events: l1 — link 1 lights: fills with the brand gradient colour and glows
l2 — link 2 lights
l3 — link 3 lights
l4 — link 4 lights
l5 — link 5 lights
l6 — link 6 lights
l7 — link 7 lights
l8 — link 8 lights
all — every link lights in sequence left to right as a quick wave, then the whole chain pulses once
parts.accuracy: Anchors for links beyond data.n sit on the last link. Links in the default state are soft grey outlines, clearly 'not yet'.
